overall: The AG found the Everett School Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law in the notice-sufficiency allegations for the February 2 and April 14 meetings. It separately recommended amending the February 2 executive session minutes and noted a late complaint response in footnotes.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the notice for the February 2 meeting (executive session) was not sufficiently specific; the complaint named no particular defect.
allegations.key_passage: Because the complaint did not identify what was allegedly insufficient about the notice for the February 2 meeting, we do not further investigate whether in this instance the description of the topic to be discussed at the February 2 meeting was sufficiently detailed.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the notice for the April 14 meeting (16 topics) was not sufficiently specific; the complaint named no particular defect.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the topics listed on each notice are not clearly insufficient on their face

allegations.summary: Whether the February 2 notice gave a sufficient purpose for the Purpose 3 (collective bargaining/litigation) executive session.
allegations.key_passage: Moreover, the notice of the February 2 meeting included the specific statutory citation of the executive session the Committee planned to convene under and therefore provided a sufficient description of the executive session purpose.

allegations.summary: The April 14 notice lacked the meeting time on its face; a cover letter posted with it stated the time.
allegations.key_passage: We, therefore, find that the Committee substantially complied with the Open Meeting Law

allegations.summary: Second complaint suggested the April 14 notice lacked the date and time it was posted; the AG checked the posting record.
allegations.key_passage: The notice that was posted to the municipal website, which is the official method of notice posting for the City of Everett, included a date and time stamp by the City Clerk

allegations.summary: Not alleged by complainants; AG reviewed the February 2 executive session minutes in camera and found them likely too thin.
allegations.key_passage: we note that the minutes appear inadequate to meet the standard required by the Open Meeting Law because they do not offer a sufficiently detailed summary of the Committee

remedy: Amend the February 2 executive session minutes in accordance with G.L. c. 30A, § 22(a) (recommendation, not a formal order).
remedy_passage: We recommend that the Committee amend its February 2 executive session meeting minutes in accordance with the requirements of G.L. c. 30A, § 22(a).
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
